rule_title: One coherent thematic improvement per round
message: The single commit 9ca82ff bundles at least four distinct themes — pricing/cost accounting (stepback/pricing.py +562), shim instrumentation (stepback/shims.py +654 new), parallel branch fan-out/join (tests/fixtures/parallel_agent.py + tests/test_parallel_branches.py), and trace compression (tests/test_compression.py). Each ships its own test file, indicating these are independent features rather than one coherent expansion. Rule 2 forbids bundling unrelated improvements even though each individually may be virtuous.
evidence: git diff HEAD~1 HEAD --stat shows: stepback/pricing.py +562, stepback/shims.py +654 (new), tests/test_pricing.py +325, tests/test_shims.py +507, tests/test_parallel_branches.py +206, tests/test_compression.py +315
Four new top-level test files (test_pricing, test_shims, test_parallel_branches, test_compression) each cover an independent subsystem

rule_title: Tests come with features (and Rule 3a: end-to-end fixture testing)
message: Tests were added with the features (good), but tests/fixtures/ contains only synthetic Python-authored agents (parallel_agent.py, agent.py) — no real recorded trace fixture from an actual LLM/tool session is committed. Rule 3a calls for at least one e2e test using a REAL fixture per round; for a record/replay library this would be a recorded trace JSON from an actual agent run. Synthetic fake_llm fixtures don't exercise the real end-goal pipeline.
evidence: tests/fixtures/parallel_agent.py defines a `fake_llm` helper rather than loading a recorded trace
ls tests/fixtures/ → __init__.py, agent.py, parallel_agent.py (no .json/.jsonl trace fixtures)

message: The commit checks in binary build artifacts that should never be tracked: .DS_Store (modified, +2KB) and 18 __pycache__/*.pyc files (both cpython-311 and cpython-314 variants for every module and test). There is no .gitignore in the repo. This bloats diffs, creates merge churn between developer machines, and violates standard Python project hygiene. While not an explicit numbered constitution rule, it undermines the auditability the constitutional/critic round depends on (real source diff signal vs. byte-level pyc churn).
evidence: git diff HEAD~1 HEAD --stat: '.DS_Store | Bin 8196 -> 10244 bytes'
git diff HEAD~1 HEAD --stat lists 14 stepback/__pycache__/*.pyc + 8 tests/__pycache__/*.pyc + 2 tests/fixtures/__pycache__/*.pyc entries

rule_title: OPENAI_API_KEY boundary / agent CLI for reasoning (runbook fc7a0f)
message: Could not verify either way from the diff alone, but the new pricing.py (+562 LOC) and shims.py (+654 LOC) appear to implement provider-side cost/token logic. If they include any direct OpenAI SDK reasoning calls (chat.completions, etc.) that should route through the agent CLI per CONSTITUTION rule 6, that would be a violation. Reviewer should grep the new modules for `openai.` / `chat.completions` / `anthropic.` to confirm they only intercept calls rather than originate reasoning.
evidence: stepback/pricing.py grew from ~30 LOC to 562 LOC in a single commit
